title: Asahi owner MFA approval and audit with independent PostgreSQL logins
scope: Signed synthetic OIDC IdP through HTTPS-origin TestClient, Postgres 16 two-password login challenge, proof and approval audit; excludes public HTTPS ingress, customer IdP and delivery.
environment: disposable PostgreSQL 16 GitHub Actions CI (synthetic ID token; not deployed HTTPS staging)

criteria.given: Active tenant owner session and fresh RS256 signed synthetic MFA token
criteria.when: Browser BFF starts OIDC flow and completes callback
criteria.then: Approval policy created once using dedicated issuer and approver PostgreSQL login credentials; audit operation 'created' is persisted

criteria.given: Approved delivery policy and fresh signed synthetic MFA
criteria.when: Owner initiates revoke and completes callback
criteria.then: Policy disabled with one 'revoked' audit operation

criteria.given: Invalid MFA, stale auth_time, forged state/tenant or revoked session
criteria.then: No unauthorized approval or audit record; cross-role privilege escalation rejected

criteria.given: Real HTTPS staging with a registered external IdP and hardened dedicated DB/TLS credentials
criteria.when: Tenant owner completes approval in real browser and restarts service
criteria.then: Fresh MFA verified, persistent change survives restart and owner independently accepts the flow

blockers: No external IdP or real HTTPS ingress/PKCE browser login has been exercised
No distributed throttling, production-grade secrets, verified PostgreSQL TLS or restart/rollback acceptance
No durable approved browser screenshots or independent owner sign-off
